title: NeoHorse-1: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement via Agentic Post-Training with Routing Harness
data_curation: The primary corpus is on the order of 10^5-10^6 trajectories produced by a deployed routing harness (heterogeneous model pool plus harnesses such as OpenSquilla), supplemented by public data (OASST2, Aya, OpenThoughts3, OpenR1-Math, ToolACE, APIGen, Nemotron-SFT-SWE-v3, HelpSteer2, UltraFeedback). Data is organized as trajectory -> user turn (training unit) -> subscene (adjacent turns sharing a local goal). Pipeline: exact/near-dup dedup and decontamination against every eval suite; rule-based structural validation (causal order, tool-call/result closure) sorting trajectories into complete, partially recoverable (only causally closed sub-trajectories kept) or quarantined; six-dimension semantic evaluation (goal attainment, instruction adherence, tool use, evidence consistency, error recovery, termination) graded PASS/WARN/FAIL/NOT_EVALUATED by deterministic checks plus an evidence-restricted judge; subscene labeling on Scene/Goal/Outcome axes. Each turn also keeps the router's raw C0-C3 tier prediction, the policy-adjusted decision and the tier actually served.
curriculum: SFT runs as a three-stage routing-guided curriculum: each stage holds roughly one third of the examples, ordered by a routing score (hard tier index k_i, or soft score s_i = sum_k k*pi_i,k over C0-C3), progressively adding higher-demand examples while reserving some low-score examples for later stages. Every example is used once per pass, with no optimizer or LR-schedule reset between stages. Routing-guided on-policy distillation follows with the same three-stage context allocation (distribution rho_j over starting contexts, j=1..3). Outside training, a capability-guided allocation step evaluates each checkpoint on a decontaminated stratified suite, builds a model-deficiency profile and shifts the next mixture toward weak regions (an evaluation-selection-update loop); the paper runs only one pass of this loop.
method: Base models are Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen3.5-9B. Agentic SFT serializes each user turn with the Qwen3.5 chat template: reasoning from the current turn is kept, earlier-turn reasoning is dropped, and earlier visible responses and tool I/O stay as context. A binary loss mask supervises only current-turn assistant spans (reasoning, tool calls, visible text, EOS), normalized by supervised-token count across the batch. Routing scores are re-estimated from the pre-response context rather than taken from the served model, because served routes also reflect user overrides and deployment policy. Routing-guided OPD: the student generates one response per recorded context, and a fixed teacher scores it under its own native template with aligned token IDs. The loss is a response-normalized reverse KL over coarsened top-K+1 distributions (the student's top-K tokens plus one remainder bin), and the rollout checkpoint is refreshed during training. Separately, NeoHorse-Jev-4B adapts the 4B model into a prefill-only decision model with a learned readout (based on Kev) that returns Choice/Noul/Score decisions with probabilities.
eval_metrics: Ten benchmarks. Agentic: QwenClawBench, PinchBench (both run in the OpenSquilla harness), WorkBuddy Bench, VitaBench (DeepSeek-V4-Flash as user simulator and judge), BFCL V4, tau2-Bench (Airline/Retail/Telecom). Coding: HumanEval, LiveCodeBench v6. Instruction following: IFEval, IFBench. All models run in thinking mode with Qwen3.5 sampling (T=1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20, presence penalty 1.5), max output 51,200 or 32,768 tokens, and 3-run means on QwenClaw, WorkBuddy and tau2. 4B (Qwen3.5-4B -> NeoHorse-1-4B): BFCL 61.02->61.79, tau2 84.29->88.46, HumanEval 87.20->96.95, LCB v6 53.71->59.43, macro avg 58.94->64.87. 9B: tau2 88.04->90.82, BFCL 64.88->67.43, IFEval 89.46->89.09, avg 65.60->69.04. NeoHorse-Jev-4B reaches a 77.70 six-group aggregate (JevBench, Kev, OpenJev text, Nimble, VitaminC, MASSIVE).
key_results: Agentic post-training raises the 10-benchmark macro average from 58.94 to 64.87 (4B) and from 65.60 to 69.04 (9B), nearly closing the gap between the post-trained 4B and the 9B base. Under a matched recipe, routing-harness data beats public Toucan tool-agent data by +6.26 avg (tau2 +11.31, HumanEval +8.54), and adding nested routing-harness supervision raises the 5-benchmark dev average monotonically from 69.31 to 71.45.
evolution_note: NeoHorse-1 extends the authors' Agentic Routing 'harness-native data flywheel' and trajectory-SFT lines (FireAct, AgentTuning, Agent-FLAN), combining them with on-policy distillation (Agarwal et al.; Thinking Machines). It reframes deployment logs as the feedback channel for recursive self-improvement, using router capability-demand predictions as a cheap difficulty signal for curriculum ordering instead of explicit difficulty labels. The authors present it as a single-iteration prototype: whether gains compound across repeated harness-to-training loops is left to future work.
